E is a positive-dimensional finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space; d=dim_R E. The nonnegative real kappa satisfies kappa>=1. V:E->R is C2 and kappa^(-1)*norm(w)^2<=D2V(x)[w,w]<=norm(w)^2 for every x,w. This is the normalized beta=1 setting.
The full state S=NNReal x E x E x Nat x (Nat->E) is written s=(b,u,xref,k,history). eta:S->R is measurable,0<eta_s<=c,0<c<1/4,0<Delta<=1/2. The initial state s0 is arbitrary and M:S->E is any actual Markov kernel. No initial-history origin,reference admissibility,stage approximation or moment guarantee is assumed.
Write K(r)=(1+r)/(kappa^(-1)+r),tau_s=K(b_s) if K(b_s)>=2 and c otherwise,L=2+log(K(b_s0)*d*2/Delta),B=(1/1024)/(sqrt(d*L)+L),J=ceil(8*log(exp(1)*K(b_s0)/B)),eps=Delta/sqrt(J+1). Real inverses and square roots use their total Lean definitions; the proof establishes the required positive denominators.
For p=(s,(x,z)),set v_s=(eta_s+tau_s)/(1+b_s),bp_s=b_s+toNNReal(v_s^(-1)),obs(p)=x+sqrt(tau_s/(1+b_s))*z,center(p)=bp_s^(-1)*(b_s*u_s+v_s^(-1)*obs(p)),F_p(w)=V(w)+bp_s/2*norm(w-center(p))^2 and D_p(w)=w-(1+bp_s)^(-1)*grad F_p(w). N_p is the least n with norm(grad F_p(D_p^n(x)))^2<=(kappa^(-1)+bp_s)*d,or0 if no such n exists. U(p)=(bp_s,center(p),D_p^N_p(x),k+1,prepend(obs(p),history)). The actual reference starts at the pre-noise x.
For the terminal program,bb_s=max(b_s,B^(-1)),A_s=bb_s^(-1),TF_s(w)=V(w)+bb_s/2*norm(w-u_s)^2 and TD_s(w)=w-(1+bb_s)^(-1)*grad TF_s(w). TN_s is the least n with norm(grad TF_s(TD_s^n(xref_s)))^2<=d*bb_s,or0 if none exists. Put xp_s=TD_s^TN_s(xref_s),g_s=grad V(xp_s),h_s=u_s-A_s*g_s.
For an auxiliary draw a=(t,z) and terminal candidate x,let theta=pi*t/2 and Z=sqrt(A_s)*z. Define W_s(x,a)=clip[-1,1](inner((pi/2)*(cos(theta)*(x-h_s)-sin(theta)*Z),g_s-grad V(h_s+sin(theta)*(x-h_s)+cos(theta)*Z))). The auxiliary law nu is volume restricted to(0,1] times standardGaussian; the proposal q_s is the law of h_s+sqrt(A_s)*Z0 for standardGaussian Z0.
One terminal attempt independently draws X~q_s,N~Poisson(2),an infinite iid nu sequence a_i,and U~Uniform[0,1]. It accepts when U<=product(i<N,(1+W_s(X,a_i))/2),with empty product1. rho_s is the law of an infinite iid sequence of such attempts. O_s returns X from the first accepted attempt,or the zero vector if no attempt accepts. This is the actual terminal stream program,with its full independent-product law.
Let muV=volume.tilted(-V),using canonical volume. Gaussian smoothing G(mu,sigma) is the law of X+sigma*Z under mu times standardGaussian. Tilt is the total normalized exponential reweighting operation; probability is proved,not implicit. Kernel composition Lt composed P first draws a state from P then an output from Lt. KL and nonnegative integrals take extended nonnegative values,possibly infinity.
muV is a probability measure. There exist Markov kernels Lt:S->E,P:S->S,TG:S->E and H:S->E such that P_s=dirac_s when B^(-1)<=b_s and otherwise P_s is the law of U(s,(X,Z)) under M_s times standardGaussian; the actual terminal stream output law (rho_s).map O_s equals Lt_s; TG_s=muV.tilted(x->-(b_s/2)*norm(x-u_s)^2); and H_s=G(TG_s,sqrt(v_s)). Define Q_s=G(M_s,sqrt(tau_s/(1+b_s))) and e(s)=0 when B^(-1)<=b_s,otherwise KL(Q_s||H_s). Then e is measurable,and for every natural m,KL((Lt composed P^(J+m))(s0)||TG_s0)<=sum(j<J,the nonnegative integral of e under(P^j)(s0))+Delta^2/(J+1). The final real term is embedded in the extended nonnegative reals.

∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : MeasurableSpace E] [inst_1 : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_2 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E]
  [inst_3 : FiniteDimensional ℝ E] [inst_4 : BorelSpace E] {V : E → ℝ} (κ : NNReal),
  1 ≤ κ →
    ContDiff ℝ 2 V →
      (∀ (x w : E), (↑κ)⁻¹ * ‖w‖ ^ 2 ≤ ((fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x) w) w ∧ ((fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ V) x) w) w ≤ ‖w‖ ^ 2) →
        0 < Module.finrank ℝ E →
          ∀ (η : NNReal × E × E × ℕ × (ℕ → E) → ℝ),
            Measurable η →
              ∀ (c Δ : ℝ),
                0 < c →
                  c < 1 / 4 →
                    (∀ (s : NNReal × E × E × ℕ × (ℕ → E)), 0 < η s ∧ η s ≤ c) →
                      0 < Δ →
                        Δ ≤ 1 / 2 →
                          ∀ (s0 : NNReal × E × E × ℕ × (ℕ → E))
                            (M : ProbabilityTheory.Kernel (NNReal × E × E × ℕ × (ℕ → E)) E)
                            [ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel M],
                            have d := ↑(Module.finrank ℝ E);
                            have K := fun r => (1 + r) / ((↑κ)⁻¹ + r);
                            have τ := fun s => if 2 ≤ K ↑s.1 then K ↑s.1 else c;
                            have L := 2 + Real.log (K ↑s0.1 * d * 2 / Δ);
                            have B := 1 / 1024 / (√(d * L) + L);
                            have J := ⌈8 * Real.log (Real.exp 1 * K ↑s0.1 / B)⌉₊;
                            have _eps := Δ / √(↑J + 1);
                            have v := fun s => (η s + τ s) / (1 + ↑s.1);
                            have bp := fun s => s.1 + (v s)⁻¹.toNNReal;
                            have obs := fun p => p.2.1 + √(τ p.1 / (1 + ↑p.1.1)) • p.2.2;
                            have center := fun p => (↑(bp p.1))⁻¹ • (↑p.1.1 • p.1.2.1 + (v p.1)⁻¹ • obs p);
                            have F := fun p x => V x + ↑(bp p.1) / 2 * ‖x - center p‖ ^ 2;
                            have T := fun p x => x - (1 + ↑(bp p.1))⁻¹ • gradient (F p) x;
                            have Qn := fun n p => ‖gradient (F p) ((T p)^[n] p.2.1)‖ ^ 2;
                            have N := fun s =>
                              if h : ∃ n, Qn n s ≤ (fun p => ((↑κ)⁻¹ + ↑(bp p.1)) * d) s then Nat.find h else 0;
                            have update := fun p =>
                              (bp p.1, center p, (T p)^[N p] p.2.1, p.1.2.2.2.1 + 1, fun n =>
                                Nat.casesOn n (obs p) p.1.2.2.2.2);
                            have bb := fun s => Max.max (↑s.1) B⁻¹;
                            have TF := fun s x => V x + bb s / 2 * ‖x - s.2.1‖ ^ 2;
                            have TT := fun s x => x - (1 + bb s)⁻¹ • gradient (TF s) x;
                            have TQn := fun n s => ‖gradient (TF s) ((TT s)^[n] s.2.2.1)‖ ^ 2;
                            have TN := fun s => if h : ∃ n, TQn n s ≤ (fun s => d * bb s) s then Nat.find h else 0;
                            have txp := fun s => (TT s)^[TN s] s.2.2.1;
                            have TA := fun s => (bb s)⁻¹;
                            have tg := fun s => gradient V (txp s);
                            have th := fun s => s.2.1 - TA s • tg s;
                            have tnu :=
                              (MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.restrict (Set.Ioc 0 1)).prod
                                (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E);
                            have tW := fun s p =>
                              Min.min 1
                                (Max.max (-1)
                                  (have s_1 := ((s, p.1), p.2).1.1;
                                  have x := ((s, p.1), p.2).1.2;
                                  have t := ((s, p.1), p.2).2.1;
                                  have z := √(TA s_1) • ((s, p.1), p.2).2.2;
                                  Inner.inner ℝ
                                    ((Real.pi / 2) •
                                      (Real.cos (Real.pi / 2 * t) • (x - th s_1) - Real.sin (Real.pi / 2 * t) • z))
                                    (tg s_1 -
                                      gradient V
                                        (th s_1 + Real.sin (Real.pi / 2 * t) • (x - th s_1) +
                                          Real.cos (Real.pi / 2 * t) • z))));
                            have tproposal := fun s =>
                              MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun z => th s + √(TA s) • z) (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E);
                            have trho := fun s =>
                              MeasureTheory.Measure.infinitePi fun x =>
                                (tproposal s).prod
                                  ((ProbabilityTheory.poissonMeasure
                                        ⟨2 * 1,
                                          le_of_lt
                                            (mul_pos
                                              (Mathlib.Meta.Positivity.pos_of_isNat
                                                (Mathlib.Meta.NormNum.isNat_ofNat ℝ (Eq.refl 2))
                                                (Eq.refl (Nat.ble 1 2)))
                                              (Mathlib.Meta.NormNum.isNat_lt_true
                                                (Mathlib.Meta.NormNum.isNat_ofNat ℝ Nat.cast_zero)
                                                (Mathlib.Meta.NormNum.isNat_ofNat ℝ Nat.cast_one)
                                                (Eq.refl Bool.false)))⟩).prod
                                    ((MeasureTheory.Measure.infinitePi fun x => tnu).prod
                                      (MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.restrict (Set.Icc 0 1))));
                            have _tpi := fun s =>
                              (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun z => s.2.1 + √(TA s) • z)
                                    (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)).tilted
                                fun x => -V x;
                            have μV := MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume.tilted fun x => -V x;
                            MeasureTheory.IsProbabilityMeasure μV ∧
                              ∃ Lt P TG H,
                                ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel Lt ∧
                                  ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel P ∧
                                    ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel TG ∧
                                      ProbabilityTheory.IsMarkovKernel H ∧
                                        (∀ (s : NNReal × E × E × ℕ × (ℕ → E)),
                                            P s =
                                              if B⁻¹ ≤ ↑s.1 then MeasureTheory.Measure.dirac s
                                              else
                                                MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun z => update (s, z))
                                                  ((M s).prod (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E))) ∧
                                          (∀ (s : NNReal × E × E × ℕ × (ℕ → E)),
                                              MeasureTheory.Measure.map
                                                  (fun omega =>
                                                    if h :
                                                        ∃ n,
                                                          omega n ∈
                                                            {p |
                                                              p.2.2.2 ≤
                                                                ∏ i, (1 + tW s (p.1, p.2.2.1 ↑i)) / (2 * 1)} then
                                                      (omega (Nat.find h)).1
                                                    else 0)
                                                  (trho s) =
                                                Lt s) ∧
                                            (∀ (s : NNReal × E × E × ℕ × (ℕ → E)),
                                                TG s = μV.tilted fun x => -(↑s.1 / 2) * ‖x - s.2.1‖ ^ 2) ∧
                                              (∀ (s : NNReal × E × E × ℕ × (ℕ → E)),
                                                  H s =
                                                    MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun p => p.1 + p.2)
                                                      ((TG s).prod
                                                        (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun z => √(v s) • z)
                                                          (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)))) ∧
                                                have Q := fun s =>
                                                  MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun p => p.1 + p.2)
                                                    ((M s).prod
                                                      (MeasureTheory.Measure.map (fun z => √(τ s / (1 + ↑s.1)) • z)
                                                        (ProbabilityTheory.stdGaussian E)));
                                                have e := fun s =>
                                                  if B⁻¹ ≤ ↑s.1 then 0 else InformationTheory.klDiv (Q s) (H s);
                                                Measurable e ∧
                                                  ∀ (m : ℕ),
                                                    InformationTheory.klDiv ((Lt.comp (P ^ (J + m))) s0) (TG s0) ≤
                                                      ∑ j ∈ Finset.range J,
                                                          ∫⁻ (s : NNReal × E × E × ℕ × (ℕ → E)), e s ∂(P ^ j) s0 +
                                                        ENNReal.ofReal (Δ ^ 2 / (↑J + 1))

Let \(E\) be a finite-dimensional real inner-product space, equipped with its normed additive-group structure and its Borel measurable-space structure. Let \(V:E\to\mathbb R\), and let \(\kappa\in\mathbb R_{\ge0}\). Assume
\[
1\le\kappa,\qquad V\in C^2(E;\mathbb R),
\]
and, for every \(x,w\in E\),
\[
\kappa^{-1}\|w\|^2
\le D^2V(x)[w,w]\le \|w\|^2.
\]
Assume the real dimension
\[
d=\dim_{\mathbb R}E
\]
is strictly positive. In formulas below, \(d\) denotes this dimension cast to a real number, and nonnegative-real state coordinates and \(\kappa\) are likewise cast to reals where needed.

The state space is
\[
S=\mathbb R_{\ge0}\times E\times E\times\mathbb N\times E^{\mathbb N}.
\]
Write a state as \(s=(b,a,x,k,h)\), where \(h:\mathbb N\to E\) is a full infinite sequence. Let \(\eta:S\to\mathbb R\) be measurable. Let \(c,\Delta\in\mathbb R\) satisfy
\[
0<c<\tfrac14,\qquad
\forall s\in S,\quad 0<\eta(s)\le c,\qquad
0<\Delta\le\tfrac12.
\]
Fix any initial state \(s_0=(b_0,a_0,x_0,k_0,h_0)\), without further restrictions, and any Markov kernel \(M:S\rightsquigarrow E\). In particular, no approximation-quality, absolute-continuity, or finite-relative-entropy assumption is imposed on \(M\).

Define
\[
K(r)=\frac{1+r}{\kappa^{-1}+r},
\qquad
\tau(s)=
\begin{cases}
K(b),&2\le K(b),\\
c,&K(b)<2,
\end{cases}
\]
and
\[
L=2+\log\!\left(\frac{2K(b_0)d}{\Delta}\right),\qquad
B=\frac{1/1024}{\sqrt{dL}+L},
\]
\[
J=\left\lceil 8\log\!\left(\frac{eK(b_0)}B\right)\right\rceil_{\mathbb N},
\qquad
\varepsilon=\frac{\Delta}{\sqrt{J+1}}.
\]
The displayed natural ceiling is the total natural-number ceiling operation. The local name \(\varepsilon\) does not occur subsequently in the formal conclusion.

For each \(s=(b,a,x,k,h)\), define
\[
v(s)=\frac{\eta(s)+\tau(s)}{1+b},\qquad
b^+(s)=b+\operatorname{toNNReal}\!\left(v(s)^{-1}\right).
\]
Here \(\operatorname{toNNReal}\) truncates below at zero. Keep this operation as displayed rather than silently replacing it in the formal specification.

For \(p=(s,(y,z))\in S\times(E\times E)\), define
\[
o(p)=y+\sqrt{\frac{\tau(s)}{1+b}}\,z,
\]
\[
a^+(p)=b^+(s)^{-1}\bigl(ba+v(s)^{-1}o(p)\bigr),
\]
\[
F_p(u)=V(u)+\frac{b^+(s)}2\|u-a^+(p)\|^2,
\qquad
T_p(u)=u-\frac{1}{1+b^+(s)}\nabla F_p(u).
\]
Inverses involving \(b^+(s)\) above use its real coercion. Set
\[
q_n(p)=\left\|\nabla F_p\!\left(T_p^{\,n}(y)\right)\right\|^2
\]
and define the total first-hit index
\[
N(p)=
\begin{cases}
\min\{n\in\mathbb N:q_n(p)\le(\kappa^{-1}+b^+(s))d\},
&\text{if this set is nonempty},\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Define the state update
\[
U(p)=\bigl(b^+(s),\,a^+(p),\,T_p^{\,N(p)}(y),\,k+1,\,h^+(p)\bigr),
\]
where
\[
h^+(p)(0)=o(p),\qquad h^+(p)(n+1)=h(n).
\]
Thus this iteration starts at the newly sampled \(y\), not at the third coordinate \(x\) of the incoming state.

The terminal construction uses, for each state \(s=(b,a,x,k,h)\),
\[
\bar b(s)=\max\{b,B^{-1}\},
\]
\[
F_s^{\mathrm t}(u)=V(u)+\frac{\bar b(s)}2\|u-a\|^2,
\qquad
T_s^{\mathrm t}(u)=u-\frac{1}{1+\bar b(s)}\nabla F_s^{\mathrm t}(u),
\]
\[
q_n^{\mathrm t}(s)
=\left\|\nabla F_s^{\mathrm t}\!\left((T_s^{\mathrm t})^n(x)\right)\right\|^2,
\]
\[
N^{\mathrm t}(s)=
\begin{cases}
\min\{n\in\mathbb N:q_n^{\mathrm t}(s)\le d\bar b(s)\},
&\text{if this set is nonempty},\\
0,&\text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}
\]
Then set
\[
x^{\mathrm t}(s)=(T_s^{\mathrm t})^{N^{\mathrm t}(s)}(x),
\quad
A(s)=\bar b(s)^{-1},
\quad
g(s)=\nabla V(x^{\mathrm t}(s)),
\quad
\theta(s)=a-A(s)g(s).
\]
This terminal iteration starts at the third state coordinate \(x\).

Let \(\gamma_E\) denote standard Gaussian measure on \(E\), and let
\[
\nu=\bigl(\mathrm{Leb}_{\mathbb R}|_{(0,1]}\bigr)\otimes\gamma_E.
\]
For a candidate \(y\in E\) and an auxiliary pair \((t,z_0)\in\mathbb R\times E\), put \(z=\sqrt{A(s)}\,z_0\) and define
\[
\begin{split}
W_s(y,(t,z_0))
=\min\Biggl\{1,\max\Biggl\{-1,\,
\Biggl\langle&
\frac{\pi}{2}\left(
\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)(y-\theta(s))
-\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)z
\right),\\
&g(s)-\nabla V\!\left(
\theta(s)
+\sin\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)(y-\theta(s))
+\cos\!\left(\frac{\pi t}{2}\right)z
\right)
\Biggr\rangle_{\mathbb R}
\Biggr\}\Biggr\}.
\end{split}
\]
The expression is explicitly clipped to \([-1,1]\).

Define the candidate law
\[
R_s=(z\mapsto\theta(s)+\sqrt{A(s)}\,z)_\#\gamma_E.
\]
One trial is a tuple
\[
p=(Y,N,((T_i,Z_i))_{i\in\mathbb N},U)
\]
with independent coordinates distributed according to
\[
R_s\otimes
\left(
\operatorname{Poisson}(2)\otimes
\left(\nu^{\otimes\mathbb N}
\otimes(\mathrm{Leb}_{\mathbb R}|_{[0,1]})\right)
\right).
\]
The tuple grouping in this expression is the grouping of the displayed nested products. Let \(\rho_s\) be the independent countable product of this trial law. Thus \(\omega\) is an infinite sequence of independent trials.

Declare a trial accepted exactly when
\[
U\le
\prod_{i=0}^{N-1}\frac{1+W_s(Y,(T_i,Z_i))}{2}.
\]
The product is \(1\) for \(N=0\). Define the total output function
\[
\mathcal A_s(\omega)=
\begin{cases}
Y_{n_*},&
n_*=\min\{n\in\mathbb N:\omega_n\text{ is accepted}\}
\text{ exists},\\
0_E,&\text{if no trial is accepted}.
\end{cases}
\]

A further local measure is defined in the statement:
\[
\pi_s^{\mathrm t}
=
\left((z\mapsto a+\sqrt{A(s)}z)_\#\gamma_E\right)
.\operatorname{tilted}(-V).
\]
This local measure is unused in the asserted conclusion; in particular, there is no displayed assertion identifying the terminal output law with \(\pi_s^{\mathrm t}\).

Let
\[
\mu_V=\mathrm{Leb}_E.\operatorname{tilted}(-V),
\]
where `tilted` is the given total normalized exponential-reweighting operation.

The theorem concludes that \(\mu_V\) is a probability measure and that there exist Markov kernels
\[
L_{\mathrm t}:S\rightsquigarrow E,\qquad
P:S\rightsquigarrow S,\qquad
TG:S\rightsquigarrow E,\qquad
H:S\rightsquigarrow E
\]
with all of the following properties.

For every state \(s=(b,a,x,k,h)\),
\[
P(s)=
\begin{cases}
\delta_s,&B^{-1}\le b,\\
U(s,\cdot)_\#\bigl(M(s)\otimes\gamma_E\bigr),&b<B^{-1}.
\end{cases}
\]
The Gaussian used here is independent of the draw \(y\sim M(s)\). Above the threshold the entire state is fixed, including its counter and history sequence.

For every state \(s\),
\[
L_{\mathrm t}(s)=(\mathcal A_s)_\#\rho_s,
\]
\[
TG(s)=
\mu_V.\operatorname{tilted}
\left(u\mapsto-\frac b2\|u-a\|^2\right),
\]
and
\[
H(s)=
(u,w\mapsto u+w)_\#
\left[
TG(s)\otimes
(z\mapsto\sqrt{v(s)}z)_\#\gamma_E
\right].
\]

Define
\[
Q(s)=
(u,w\mapsto u+w)_\#
\left[
M(s)\otimes
\left(z\mapsto
\sqrt{\frac{\tau(s)}{1+b}}z\right)_\#\gamma_E
\right]
\]
and the extended-nonnegative error
\[
e(s)=
\begin{cases}
0,&B^{-1}\le b,\\
\operatorname{KL}(Q(s)\|H(s)),&b<B^{-1}.
\end{cases}
\]
The theorem asserts that \(e\) is measurable and, for every \(m\in\mathbb N\),
\[
\boxed{
\operatorname{KL}
\left(
(L_{\mathrm t}\circ P^{\,J+m})(s_0)
\,\middle\|\,TG(s_0)
\right)
\le
\sum_{j=0}^{J-1}
\int_S^{-}e(s)\,d(P^j(s_0))(s)
+
\operatorname{ofReal}_{\mathbb R_{\ge0}\cup\{\infty\}}
\left(\frac{\Delta^2}{J+1}\right).
}
\]
Here composition means first applying \(P^{J+m}\), then \(L_{\mathrm t}\). Kernel exponent zero is the identity kernel, so \(P^0(s_0)=\delta_{s_0}\). The target on the left is the measure \(TG(s_0)\) at the original initial state. The sum on the right stops at \(J-1\), independently of \(m\).

All KL divergences and displayed nonnegative integrals take values in the extended nonnegative reals. The assertion includes the possibility of infinite KL or an infinite right-hand side; it contains no implicit finiteness or absolute-continuity hypothesis. When the right-hand side is finite, the inequality bounds the final KL by that finite quantity; when it is infinite, the displayed inequality remains an extended-real assertion.

The statement retains three explicit fallback branches: the ordinary gradient-iteration first hit defaults to \(0\) if absent, the terminal gradient-iteration first hit defaults to \(0\) if absent, and the repeated-trial output defaults to \(0_E\) if there is no accepted trial. There is no separate displayed termination-probability, iteration-count, expected-cost, or runtime bound. The existence of the asserted Markov kernels includes probability of their fibers, but the text does not separately assert that these fallback events are null.

The constants \(L,B,J\) depend on \(\kappa,d,b_0,\Delta\); \(\tau\) also uses \(c\), and \(v\) uses \(\eta\). The transition kernel can depend on every state coordinate through arbitrary measurable \(\eta\) and \(M\), including the full history sequence and counter. No finite-memory restriction is imposed.

private theorem kl_le_second_moment {X : Type*} [MeasurableSpace X]
    (μ ν : Measure X) [IsProbabilityMeasure μ] [IsProbabilityMeasure ν]
    (hac : μ ≪ ν) (eps : ℝ)
    (hI : Integrable (fun x => ((μ.rnDeriv ν x).toReal)^2) ν)
    (hB : (∫ x, ((μ.rnDeriv ν x).toReal)^2 ∂ν) ≤ 1+eps^2) :
    klDiv μ ν ≤ ENNReal.ofReal (eps^2) := by

    simpa [r] using Measure.integrableOn_toReal_rnDeriv

  have hmass : (∫ x, r x ∂ν) = 1 := by
    simpa [r] using Measure.integral_toReal_rnDeriv hac

  have hlin : Integrable (fun x => 2*r x) ν := hr.const_mul 2
  have hpoly : Integrable (fun x => r x^2-2*r x) ν := h2.sub hlin
  have heq : (fun x => (r x-1)^2) = (fun x => r x^2-2*r x+1) := by

    linarith
  rw [klDiv_eq_lintegral_klFun_of_ac hac]

      apply lintegral_mono

    (f : ℕ → A → ℝ≥0∞) (hzero : ∀ s, f 0 s ≤ t s)
    (hstep : ∀ n s, f (n+1) s ≤ e s + ∫⁻ x, f n x ∂P s) :
    ∀ n s, f n s ≤ (∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, ∫⁻ x, e x ∂(P^j) s) + ∫⁻ x, t x ∂(P^n) s := by
  have hp (n : ℕ) : IsMarkovKernel (P^n) := by
    induction n with
    | zero => change IsMarkovKernel Kernel.id; infer_instance
    | succ n ih =>
      let := ih
      rw [pow_succ]
      change IsMarkovKernel ((P^n) ∘ₖ P)
      infer_instance
  let := hp
  have hi (n : ℕ) : Measurable (fun s => ∫⁻ x, e x ∂(P^n) s) := he.lintegral_kernel
  intro n
  induction n with
  | zero =>
    intro s
    simp only [Finset.range_zero,Finset.sum_empty,zero_add,pow_zero]
    change f 0 s ≤ ∫⁻ x, t x ∂Measure.dirac s
    simpa only [lintegral_dirac' s ht] using hzero s
  | succ n ih =>
    intro s
    calc
      f (n+1) s ≤ e s + ∫⁻ x, f n x ∂P s := hstep n s
      _ ≤ e s + ∫⁻ x, (∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, ∫⁻ y, e y ∂(P^j) x) +
          ∫⁻ y, t y ∂(P^n) x ∂P s := add_le_add le_rfl (lintegral_mono ih)

        rw [lintegral_add_left (Finset.measurable_sum _ (fun j _ => hi j))]
        rw [lintegral_finsetSum _ (fun j _ => hi j)]
        have hei (j : ℕ) : (∫⁻ x, ∫⁻ y, e y ∂(P^j) x ∂P s) = ∫⁻ y, e y ∂(P^(j+1)) s := by
          rw [pow_succ]

          rw [pow_succ]
          exact (Kernel.lintegral_comp (P^n) P s ht).symm

        rw [hti,Finset.sum_range_succ']
        simp only [pow_zero]
        rw [show (1 : Kernel A A) s = Measure.dirac s from rfl,lintegral_dirac' s he]
        change e s + ((∑ j ∈ Finset.range n, ∫⁻ x, e x ∂(P^(j+1)) s) + _) =

        ac_rfl

formulae.label: Actual finite output with explicit observation error

assumptions: E is a positive-dimensional finite-dimensional real inner-product Borel space; d=dim_R E. The nonnegative real kappa satisfies kappa>=1. V:E->R is C2 and kappa^(-1)*norm(w)^2<=D2V(x)[w,w]<=norm(w)^2 for every x,w. This is the normalized beta=1 setting.

The full state S=NNReal x E x E x Nat x (Nat->E) is written s=(b,u,xref,k,history). eta:S->R is measurable,0<eta_s<=c,0<c<1/4,0<Delta<=1/2. The initial state s0 is arbitrary and M:S->E is any actual Markov kernel. No initial-history origin,reference admissibility,stage approximation or moment guarantee is assumed.

Write K(r)=(1+r)/(kappa^(-1)+r),tau_s=K(b_s) if K(b_s)>=2 and c otherwise,L=2+log(K(b_s0)*d*2/Delta),B=(1/1024)/(sqrt(d*L)+L),J=ceil(8*log(exp(1)*K(b_s0)/B)),eps=Delta/sqrt(J+1). Real inverses and square roots use their total Lean definitions; the proof establishes the required positive denominators.

For p=(s,(x,z)),set v_s=(eta_s+tau_s)/(1+b_s),bp_s=b_s+toNNReal(v_s^(-1)),obs(p)=x+sqrt(tau_s/(1+b_s))*z,center(p)=bp_s^(-1)*(b_s*u_s+v_s^(-1)*obs(p)),F_p(w)=V(w)+bp_s/2*norm(w-center(p))^2 and D_p(w)=w-(1+bp_s)^(-1)*grad F_p(w). N_p is the least n with norm(grad F_p(D_p^n(x)))^2<=(kappa^(-1)+bp_s)*d,or0 if no such n exists. U(p)=(bp_s,center(p),D_p^N_p(x),k+1,prepend(obs(p),history)). The actual reference starts at the pre-noise x.

For the terminal program,bb_s=max(b_s,B^(-1)),A_s=bb_s^(-1),TF_s(w)=V(w)+bb_s/2*norm(w-u_s)^2 and TD_s(w)=w-(1+bb_s)^(-1)*grad TF_s(w). TN_s is the least n with norm(grad TF_s(TD_s^n(xref_s)))^2<=d*bb_s,or0 if none exists. Put xp_s=TD_s^TN_s(xref_s),g_s=grad V(xp_s),h_s=u_s-A_s*g_s.

For an auxiliary draw a=(t,z) and terminal candidate x,let theta=pi*t/2 and Z=sqrt(A_s)*z. Define W_s(x,a)=clip[-1,1](inner((pi/2)*(cos(theta)*(x-h_s)-sin(theta)*Z),g_s-grad V(h_s+sin(theta)*(x-h_s)+cos(theta)*Z))). The auxiliary law nu is volume restricted to(0,1] times standardGaussian; the proposal q_s is the law of h_s+sqrt(A_s)*Z0 for standardGaussian Z0.

One terminal attempt independently draws X~q_s,N~Poisson(2),an infinite iid nu sequence a_i,and U~Uniform[0,1]. It accepts when U<=product(i<N,(1+W_s(X,a_i))/2),with empty product1. rho_s is the law of an infinite iid sequence of such attempts. O_s returns X from the first accepted attempt,or the zero vector if no attempt accepts. This is the actual terminal stream program,with its full independent-product law.

Let muV=volume.tilted(-V),using canonical volume. Gaussian smoothing G(mu,sigma) is the law of X+sigma*Z under mu times standardGaussian. Tilt is the total normalized exponential reweighting operation; probability is proved,not implicit. Kernel composition Lt composed P first draws a state from P then an output from Lt. KL and nonnegative integrals take extended nonnegative values,possibly infinity.

steps.text: Actual Gibbs probability rules out a zero tilted measure. Since nonintegrable exp(-V) would make the tilt zero,it proves exponential integrability before tilted_tilted is used. steps.text: For probability mu absolutely continuous with respect to nu,set r=dmu/dnu. The RN API gives integrability of r and integral r=1. Given square integrability,expand(r-1)^2 and obtain integral(r-1)^2=integral r^2-1. For r>=0,log r<=r-1 gives klFun(r)<=(r-1)^2;the r=0 case is explicit. steps.text: Induct the all-ENNReal recurrence with nonnegative kernel integration. At zero steps,the Dirac integral is the terminal residual.
